extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and authors in mathematical/philosophical logic preparing manuscripts for submission to the Bulletin of Symbolic Logic
extracted.subtask_description: Author instructions and submission requirements for manuscripts to the Bulletin of Symbolic Logic, describing scope, acceptable article types, submission system requirements, and open-access/payment policies. Intended to guide prospective authors on what the journal publishes and how to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal scope and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic was established ... to provide a journal of high standards that would be both accessible and of interest to as wide an audience as possible. It is designed to cover all areas within the purview of the ASL: mathematical logic and its applications, philosophical and non-classical logic and its applications, history and philosophy of logic, and philosophy and methodology of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should fall within these topical areas and be written at a level accessible to a broad audience of logicians (i.e., not narrowly specialized exposition inaccessible to the ASL readership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article types accepted (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: We publish the following types of articles: Article*, Communication*, Meeting Report, Book Review, Survey*, Notes, Thesis Abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should select the appropriate article type when preparing and submitting their work; each type has different expectations (see below entries for Articles and Communications). The asterisked types may have open-access APC considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles (full papers) — suitability criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles presenting topics of broad interest in a way that is accessible to a large audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full articles should communicate material of broad interest within the ASL community and be written to be accessible rather than narrowly technical; structure and exposition should target a large, diverse readership of logicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications — suitability criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications which are announcements of important new results and ideas in any aspect of logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications are intended for concise announcements of important new results or ideas; authors should ensure significance and novelty appropriate for a short/rapid-format communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other content sections (reviews, theses, reports, notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulletin also publishes a Reviews Section, a Thesis Abstract Section and reports of ASL meetings, Notices of interest to logicians, and the annual listing of ASL officers, Council members, committee members, and individual and institutional members of the Association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions corresponding to these categories should follow the norms for those formats (e.g., book reviews, thesis abstracts, meeting reports) and be submitted under the correct category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of partner secure submission system / account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We partner with a secure submission system to handle manuscript submissions. You will need an account for the submission system, which is separate to your Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must create and use an account on the partner submission system to submit manuscripts; for login and submission support, visit the submission and support pages linked by the journal. Click 'Proceed to submission system' to continue to the partner site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read 'preparing your materials' before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Please review this journal's author instructions, particularly the preparing your materials page, before submitting your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are required to consult the preparing your materials guidance (formatting, files required, metadata, cover letter, etc.) prior to submission to avoid avoidable delays or desk rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access / APC waiver and discount policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain article types (for example, Research Articles and Surveys) may be eligible for APC waivers or discounts under one of the agreements Cambridge University Press has made to support open access. For each article or communication accepted by the Bulletin, if published Gold Open Access, all or part of the publication costs may be covered by one of the agreements Cambridge University Press has made to support open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors considering Gold Open Access should check whether their institution or funder has an agreement that covers APCs and verify eligibility for waivers/discounts for particular article types.
